texto: The law finally put a rope around Colm O'Driscoll's neck.
His boys scattered - some to other outfits, some to the rope, a few to honest work.
Saint Denis's crime boss disappeared one night; the papers never said where.
His lieutenants kept the family's grip on the city - the docks, the police, the mayor's ear.
Rains Fall led what was left of his people north, out of the Army's reach.
Dutch van der Linde's gang tore itself apart. Arthur Morgan is dead; the rest scattered.
The colonel took a post back East. A new commander holds the fort, with fewer men.
Bandits from across the river make the badlands their own - Gaptooth Ridge, Rio Bravo, Cholla Springs.
The Laramie boys run off herds from Hennigan's Stead to Blackwater, and change the brands before the owners wake.
Travellers vanish on the roads south of Saint Denis. Those who come back talk about lanterns in the trees, and the Night Folk.
New money, new streets, a bigger jail. The town wants the outlaw years forgotten.
The Lemoyne Raiders still ride the bayous - fewer every year, and angrier.
You wanna say that again? Go on.
Watch your mouth, or I'll shut it for you.
Do you know who you're talkin' to?
I've buried better men than you for less.
I don't want no trouble, mister!
Talk's cheap. Come back when you're payin'.
You're wastin' my time and my time costs money.
You don't want to do this, mister.
Dutch van der Linde killed Colm O'Driscoll's brother; Colm killed Dutch's woman, Annabelle.
Neither man has forgotten - and neither gang lets the other ride past in peace.
Banks fail from New York to Saint Denis; farms and stores go under by the hundred.
The island prison takes every road agent and rustler the law can catch.
Old Confederates who never laid down their arms ride the bayous and the fields, burning out northern money.
Men go down the mine poor and come up poorer.
Two old Scarlett Meadows families and an older feud - over land, over the war, over moonshine.
Bronte's men run the docks, the saloons and half the police.
Leviticus Cornwall's money lays track, drills oil and boils kerosene - and pays the men who do it in pennies.
Hooded fools burn crosses in the dark - and scatter the moment anyone shoots back.
Colonel Henry Favours holds Ambarino for the Army; his patrols ride the Cumberland Forest roads.
The Army hems the Wapiti onto their reservation - and oil men are already eyeing the land.
The stockyards are full and Smithfield's Saloon never closes.
The Van der Linde gang's robbery on the Blackwater ferry goes wrong - a woman is killed, and the gang runs for the mountains.
Pinkerton agents take the case; there's a price on every Van der Linde head.
They took the horses and whatever wasn't nailed down.

They burned an empty camp and two men's pride.

The bounty posters went up in Annesburg. Nobody went in after them.

The soldiers lost two men and the trail.

Nobody saw anything. Nobody ever does.

The river ran with it for a day.

His horse came home without him.

Nobody in Saint Denis would go and cut them down.

Fewer rode out than rode in.

Nobody took that road after dark for a month.

The nets were cut. The lantern was still lit.

Whatever was taken, the family won't say.

They left the city within the week.

Blackwater put a price on the brothers' heads. Nobody collected.

Only one of the hunters rode out.
Who do you ride for, and where are they holed up?
I ain't gonna ask twice. Where's your outfit camped?
You think that hurt? I'm just getting started.
I got all day. You don't.
The boss'll skin you alive for this.
You'll have to kill me first.
Spit on you, Van der Linde.

Became a father - his son is Eagle Flies
Saw the Army take the plains, treaty by broken treaty
Led his people onto the reservation in Ambarino rather than see them die fighting the Army
Speaks for his people to the soldiers at Fort Wallace and to anyone in Washington who'll listen
Still trusts in treaties and talk; his young men, Eagle Flies among them, are losing patience
Made his money in Saint Denis on the docks, in the gambling halls and the bootleg trade
Built a mansion on the bayou and filled it with paintings and fine things
Bought the police, the mayor's ear and most of the city
Calls himself a businessman; the men who cross him end up in the swamp
Owns Saint Denis - and smiles while he does it
